title: Scoring retrieval variants with a discard loop
description: This example runs four scoring variants over a fixed corpus and query set, computes mean reciprocal rank for each, and keeps only variants that improve on the current best.

steps.description: The corpus is eight short documents, each with a path, a title, and a body. The deck calls these the practice kit.
Twelve labeled queries pair a search string with the document that should rank first. These are the ground truth.
A stopword set removes common words that carry little signal.
make_scorer builds a scoring function. Three flags control it: drop stopwords, match whole words only, and weight title matches.
The inner score function splits the query, optionally filters stopwords, then counts matches in title and body. Title matches earn title_weight points; body matches earn one point.

steps.question: What does mrr return when a query's expected document never appears in the hits?
steps.answer: It returns 0 for that query because rank stays 0 and 1/rank is treated as 0.

steps.description: mrr computes mean reciprocal rank. For each query it ranks all documents by score, keeps only those with a positive score, finds the expected document's position, and adds 1/rank to the total.
Four variants are defined, each a scorer with different flags. They correspond to the rows in Model 4's table.
The loop evaluates each variant, prints its MRR to three decimals, and marks it kept if it beats the running best. The final line reports the best score and the 0.80 target.
The loop runs: baseline scores 0.667 and is kept. Attempt 1 scores 0.785 and is kept. Attempt 2 scores 0.646 and is discarded. Attempt 3 scores 0.826 and is kept as the new best.
